- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days above 80) and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast from midpoint of sentiment transition upward.
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to overfit; apply downward bias of 2–5% to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 entries (strong bullish), model often fails to account for eventual correction; add 1–2% downward adjustment at 15–20 day mark.
